description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:384-425

```rust
pub fn verify_embedded_scts(
    &self,
    leaf_cert: &Certificate,    // x509_cert::Certificate
    issuer_cert: &Certificate,
) -> Result<usize>
```

Method takes `&Certificate` from `x509-cert`. Internally, it calls
`encode_to_vec` (lines 406-413) to produce the DER bytes that the
verifier consumes. Two leakage problems:

1. `x509_cert::Certificate` is in the public method signature. If
   `pkix-ct` ever wants to swap to a different X.509 parser
   (`pkix-cert`-something, a hand-rolled parser, etc.), every
   downstream caller that passes a `Certificate` value has to
   migrate. The `x509-cert` crate is currently 0.3-pre.X; its API
   has been evolving.

2. The other verify methods (`verify_sct_for_cert`,
   `verify_sct_for_precert`) take `cert_der: &[u8]` — the
   sibling API uses bytes. The contract is split: half the verify
   methods are byte-oriented, half are parsed-cert-oriented. A
   caller cannot tell from a quick look which form to use.

Sub-problem of (1): `Certificate` is `&'a` borrowed from the
caller's owned DER. The caller already has the DER. If the verifier
needs DER too, the caller is paying:

- caller-side DER alloc (the bytes), and
- caller-side Certificate parse (~ 30-50 micros), and
- pkix-ct-side `encode_to_vec` re-encoding (~50 micros, allocation),
  and
- per-SCT cert-DER copy in the signed-input builder.

A pure byte-oriented API skips steps (b) and (c) entirely. PKIX-ppbr.7
already flags the per-SCT re-encoding cost; this is the API-contract
angle on the same issue.

Recommendation: make the bytes the only contract. Replace:

```rust
pub fn verify_embedded_scts(
    &self,
    leaf_cert_der: &[u8],
    issuer_cert_der: &[u8],
) -> Result<usize>
```

If callers want to pass a parsed `Certificate`, give them a
`&Certificate` -> `&[u8]` accessor (which `x509-cert::Certificate`
already has via TBS preservation — they keep the original DER as
`tbs_certificate.original_der_octets` or similar).

This also dissolves PKIX-ppbr.4 (the x509-cert re-encoder
bit-exactness problem): if the caller provides bytes, pkix-ct never
re-encodes the leaf bytes; the only re-encoded thing is the
extension-stripped TBS, which is what the spec defines as the
signed-over structure anyway.

Priority P2.
title: verify_embedded_scts requires parsed Certificate, re-encodes to DER internally — exposes x509-cert dep
